$comment: Skill Combination Advisor tracks. Paths are relative to skills/ and accept * wildcards (matching across folders). 'security' skills are installed with every level of the track. Edit, then run: npm run docs

1.title: Level 1 — Essentials
1.hint: Install these first. They cover the everyday work of this role and rarely conflict.

2.title: Level 2 — Professional
2.hint: Add when the project grows: production concerns, scaling and team workflows.

3.title: Level 3 — Specialist
3.hint: Add one at a time, only for the problem in front of you. These are deep and narrow.

tracks.title: Frontend Engineer
tracks.who: You build web UIs with React, Vue, Angular, Svelte or similar.
tracks.watchOut: Pick exactly one framework skill set (for example `frontend/react/*` or `frontend/vue/*`); several framework skills at once dilute routing.

tracks.title: Backend Engineer
tracks.who: You build APIs and services in any language.
tracks.watchOut: Add one stack folder only (for example `backend/nestjs/*` or `backend/go/*`). `backend-stacks` holds every framework and is meant for polyglot teams.

tracks.title: Full-Stack Product Team
tracks.who: One team owns UI, API, database and deployment.
tracks.watchOut: The `fullstack-*` bundles are broad (216–225 skills). Start from Level 1–2 here plus your stack folders, and move to a full bundle only if the agent keeps missing skills.

tracks.title: Mobile Engineer
tracks.who: You ship iOS, Android or cross-platform apps.
tracks.watchOut: Add one platform skill: `mobile/ios`, `mobile/android`, `mobile/flutter`, `mobile/react-native`, `mobile/kotlin-multiplatform`, `mobile/ionic-capacitor` or `mobile/dotnet-maui`.

tracks.title: Desktop App Engineer
tracks.who: You build native or cross-platform desktop applications.
tracks.watchOut: Level 1 and 2 are alternatives: install the one toolkit you ship with. WinUI 3 and KDE are covered inside `desktop/uwp` and `desktop/qt` references.

tracks.title: DevOps & Platform Engineer
tracks.who: You own CI/CD, infrastructure as code, Kubernetes and the internal platform.
tracks.watchOut: Add only the cloud you run on (`devops/aws`, `devops/azure`, `devops/gcp`, `devops/hetzner`, …). `devops/chaos-engineering` and `site-reliability-engineering/chaos-engineering` overlap: keep one.

tracks.title: Site Reliability Engineer
tracks.who: You own uptime, SLOs, incidents and capacity.
tracks.watchOut: `devops/incident-response` and `site-reliability-engineering/incident-response` overlap: keep the SRE one if you run formal postmortems, otherwise the DevOps one.

tracks.title: Data Engineer
tracks.who: You build pipelines, warehouses, lakes and streaming systems.
tracks.watchOut: `data/etl-pipeline` (Airflow/dbt general) and `data/etl-pipelines` (orchestration focus) overlap; start with the first.

tracks.title: ML & AI Engineer
tracks.who: You train, evaluate and serve models, or build LLM applications.
tracks.watchOut: Keep GPU kernel skills (`hardware-acceleration/*`) out unless you write kernels or tune serving; they trigger on generic performance questions.

tracks.title: AI Agent Builder
tracks.who: You build tool-using LLM agents, multi-agent systems and their harnesses.
tracks.watchOut: Read the repo rule `.claude/rules/agent-persona-design.md` with this track: it sets the tool-count and human-in-the-loop rules these skills assume.

tracks.title: Security Engineer
tracks.who: You secure applications, cloud and operations.
tracks.watchOut: Offensive skills (`advanced-security-bundle`) are educational and defensive in intent; install them only for authorized testing teams.

tracks.title: Blockchain & Web3 Engineer
tracks.who: You write smart contracts, dApps or blockchain infrastructure.
tracks.watchOut: `blockchain/blockchain-defi` and `blockchain/defi-protocols` overlap, as do `blockchain-zk` and `zero-knowledge-proofs`; keep the `blockchain-*` versions unless you need the shorter ones.

tracks.title: Game Developer
tracks.who: You build games, engines or game servers.
tracks.watchOut: Add one engine skill: `game/unity` (+ `game/game-development/unity-csharp`), `game/unreal`, `game/godot` (+ `godot-gdscript`) or `game/cocos2d`. Read `.claude/rules/game-engine-guidelines.md`.

tracks.title: Systems & Embedded Engineer
tracks.who: You write low-level, embedded, kernel or performance-critical code.
tracks.watchOut: Read `.claude/rules/misra-c-standards.md` and `.claude/rules/ebpf-safety-rules.md` with this track.

tracks.title: Software & Solution Architect
tracks.who: You design systems, write ADRs and govern architecture.
tracks.watchOut: Pair with `.claude/rules/solution-architecture.md` for the pattern catalog and ADR template.

tracks.title: Product Manager & Planner
tracks.who: You define what to build: research, specs, roadmaps and growth.
tracks.watchOut: These skills write documents; pair them with one engineering track so specs stay buildable.

tracks.title: Engineering Manager & Delivery Lead
tracks.who: You run teams, delivery, risk and stakeholders.
tracks.watchOut: `management/agile-scrum` and `management/agile-scrum-kanban` overlap; keep `agile-scrum-kanban`.

tracks.title: QA & Test Engineer
tracks.who: You own test strategy, automation and release confidence.
tracks.watchOut: `quality/e2e-testing` and `quality/quality-e2e-testing` overlap; keep `quality-e2e-testing`.

tracks.title: Designer & Design Engineer
tracks.who: You design interfaces and build design systems.
tracks.watchOut: Use `design/visual-design` section "Avoiding the Generic AI Look" whenever an agent builds UI.

tracks.title: React & Next.js Developer
tracks.who: You build React apps, usually with Next.js.
tracks.watchOut: `frontend/react/nextjs`, `frontend/nextjs/internals` and `web/nextjs-server-components` overlap; start with the first and add the others only for App Router internals.

tracks.title: Vue & Nuxt Developer
tracks.who: You build Vue 3 apps, often with Nuxt.
tracks.watchOut: Do not mix React and Vue framework skills in one project install.

tracks.title: Angular Developer
tracks.who: You build Angular applications.
tracks.watchOut: Angular projects in enterprises often pair with Java or .NET backends; add that track instead of a generic backend one.

tracks.title: Node.js & TypeScript Backend
tracks.who: You build APIs with Node.js, NestJS, Express, Fastify or Hono.
tracks.watchOut: Pick one framework (NestJS, Express, Fastify or Hono) and one ORM (Prisma or Drizzle).

tracks.title: Python Backend Developer
tracks.who: You build services with FastAPI, Django or Flask.
tracks.watchOut: Read `.claude/rules/python-uv-standards.md`: the repo standard is uv for environments and dependencies.

tracks.title: Go Backend Developer
tracks.who: You build services and tooling in Go.
tracks.watchOut: Go services often become Kubernetes controllers; add the DevOps & Platform track for that.

tracks.title: Java & Kotlin Backend Developer
tracks.who: You build JVM services with Spring Boot, Quarkus, Micronaut or Ktor.
tracks.watchOut: Spring Boot and Quarkus/Micronaut solve the same problem; install the one you run.

tracks.title: .NET Developer
tracks.who: You build services or apps with C# and .NET.
tracks.watchOut: MediatR and AutoMapper changed to commercial licenses in 2025; the dotnet skills note alternatives.

tracks.title: PHP & Ruby Web Developer
tracks.who: You build web apps with Laravel, Symfony or Rails.
tracks.watchOut: Laravel and Rails are alternatives; keep the one your project uses.

tracks.title: iOS Developer
tracks.who: You build native apps for iPhone and iPad.
tracks.watchOut: SwiftUI desktop skills (`desktop/swiftui`, `desktop/appkit`) are for macOS apps; add them only if you ship one.

tracks.title: Android Developer
tracks.who: You build native Android apps with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose.
tracks.watchOut: Kotlin Multiplatform is worth adding only when you share code with iOS.

tracks.title: Cloud Architect & Engineer
tracks.who: You design and run workloads on AWS, Azure or GCP.
tracks.watchOut: Install only the providers you use from Level 2 and 3; every extra cloud skill competes for the same requests.

tracks.title: Observability Engineer
tracks.who: You own logs, metrics, traces and alerting.
tracks.watchOut: `devops/observability`, `devops/monitoring` and `devops/apm-observability` overlap; keep `devops/observability` as the entry point and add the others only for vendor-specific work.

tracks.title: Database Engineer
tracks.who: You design schemas, tune queries and run databases at scale.
tracks.watchOut: Read `.claude/rules/database-design-standards.md` (keys, soft deletes, constraints, N+1).

tracks.title: LLM Application Developer
tracks.who: You ship features on top of LLM APIs: chat, RAG, extraction, tools.
tracks.watchOut: Read `.claude/rules/rag-vector-standards.md` before building retrieval.

tracks.title: MLOps Engineer
tracks.who: You take models from notebooks to reliable production.
tracks.watchOut: Read `.claude/rules/resource-aware-ml.md` (dtypes, serving engines, device selection).

tracks.title: Data Scientist & Analyst
tracks.who: You analyze data, run experiments and build models.
tracks.watchOut: `data-science/experimentation` and `product/ab-testing` overlap; analysts keep the first, PMs the second.

tracks.title: Application Security & DevSecOps
tracks.who: You make the software delivery pipeline and code secure.
tracks.watchOut: Pair with `.claude/rules/secure-by-default.md` and `crypto-deprecation.md`; they are the baseline these skills enforce.

tracks.title: SOC Analyst & Detection Engineer
tracks.who: You detect, investigate and respond to security incidents.
tracks.watchOut: Offensive skills are not needed for detection work; add `security/purpleteam-collaboration` instead of red-team skills.

tracks.title: Compliance & Privacy Engineer
tracks.who: You make systems meet SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA or PCI requirements.
tracks.watchOut: Skills describe controls and evidence; legal interpretation of a regulation still needs your compliance or legal team.

tracks.title: SaaS Product Builder
tracks.who: You build multi-tenant B2B or B2C SaaS.
tracks.watchOut: Tenant isolation is the top risk: check every query and cache key for the tenant id.

tracks.title: E-commerce Engineer
tracks.who: You build stores, carts, checkout and order systems.
tracks.watchOut: `ecommerce/payment-processing` and `ecommerce/payments` overlap; start with `payment-processing`.

tracks.title: Real-Time Apps Developer
tracks.who: You build chat, collaboration, live dashboards or streaming features.
tracks.watchOut: WebSockets vs SSE vs WebRTC: `backend/web-real-time` has the decision table; start there.

tracks.title: Startup CTO & Solo Founder
tracks.who: You build the first version of a product with a tiny team and little time.
tracks.watchOut: Supabase and Firebase are alternatives; pick one managed backend.

tracks.title: Tech Lead & Staff Engineer
tracks.who: You set technical direction, review code and keep quality up.
tracks.watchOut: Use `planning/create-tech-spec` for design docs; the ADR template lives in `.claude/rules/solution-architecture.md`.

tracks.title: Open-Source Maintainer
tracks.who: You run a public repository with contributors and releases.
tracks.watchOut: Public CI runs untrusted pull requests: never expose secrets to `pull_request` jobs from forks.

tracks.title: Technical Writer & Docs Engineer
tracks.who: You write READMEs, API docs, specs and changelogs.
tracks.watchOut: `backend/universal/openapi-documentation` and `devops/api-documentation` overlap; keep the backend one for spec-first work.

tracks.title: Beginner Learning Path
tracks.who: You are learning software development and want solid habits from day one.
tracks.watchOut: Learn one language well before adding a second; install Level 2 only after you have built a small project.

tracks.title: Performance Engineer
tracks.who: You make web, backend and mobile software fast.
tracks.watchOut: `quality/load-testing` and `backend/universal/load-testing` overlap; keep `quality/load-testing`.

tracks.title: Accessibility Specialist
tracks.who: You make products usable for everyone and meet WCAG.
tracks.watchOut: Automated checkers find only part of the issues; keep manual keyboard and screen-reader testing in the plan.

tracks.title: Flutter Developer
tracks.who: You build iOS and Android apps from one Dart codebase.
tracks.watchOut: Flutter golden tests need the same OS and fonts as the baseline; see `quality/visual-testing` before adding them to CI.

tracks.title: React Native Developer
tracks.who: You build mobile apps with React Native or Expo.
tracks.watchOut: React Native 0.82+ runs only on the New Architecture; `mobile/cross-platform/react-native-architecture` explains the migration.

tracks.title: Rust Developer
tracks.who: You write services, tools, desktop apps or embedded code in Rust.
tracks.watchOut: Pick the Level 3 skill that matches your target (embedded, eBPF, or low-latency) instead of installing all three.

tracks.title: Elixir & Phoenix Developer
tracks.who: You build fault-tolerant services and real-time apps on the BEAM.
tracks.watchOut: `languages/elixir` covers the language and OTP; `backend/elixir` covers Phoenix and Ecto. Install both.

tracks.title: Svelte, Solid, Astro & Qwik Developer
tracks.who: You use a newer frontend framework or a content-first site generator.
tracks.watchOut: Level 2 lists alternatives: keep only the framework you ship with (Astro for content sites, SvelteKit/Solid/Qwik/Remix for apps).

tracks.title: Unity Developer
tracks.who: You build games in Unity with C#.
tracks.watchOut: Unity DOTS (Entities) is a separate programming model; use the ECS skills only if the project adopted it.

tracks.title: Unreal Engine Developer
tracks.who: You build games or real-time 3D in Unreal Engine with C++.
tracks.watchOut: Read `.claude/rules/game-engine-guidelines.md`; its allocation and determinism rules apply to Unreal C++ too.

tracks.title: Godot Developer
tracks.who: You build games in Godot 4 with GDScript or C#.
tracks.watchOut: Godot 4 removed several Godot 3 APIs; the Godot skills flag the renamed ones (for example `SCREEN_TEXTURE`).

tracks.title: Game Engine Programmer
tracks.who: You build engine systems: rendering, memory, jobs, assets, platforms.
tracks.watchOut: Engine skills assume C++ and data-oriented design; pair with `languages/cpp` if it is not installed yet.

tracks.title: Online Game Backend Engineer
tracks.who: You run game servers, matchmaking and live-ops backends.
tracks.watchOut: `game/multiplayer-netcode` and `game/game-engine/multiplayer-netcode` overlap; start with the first.

tracks.title: Platform Engineer (IDP)
tracks.who: You build the internal developer platform and paved roads for product teams.
tracks.watchOut: `devops/kubernetes-operators` and `cloud-native/k8s-operators` overlap; keep one unless you write operators daily.

tracks.title: FinOps & Cloud Cost Engineer
tracks.who: You make cloud spend visible, accountable and lower.
tracks.watchOut: `devops/finops` and `enterprise/finops-cloud-cost` overlap; engineers keep the DevOps one, finance-facing roles the enterprise one.

tracks.title: Analytics Engineer
tracks.who: You model warehouse data with dbt and serve trusted metrics.
tracks.watchOut: dbt metrics now live in MetricFlow (semantic layer); older `metrics:` blocks in tutorials are legacy.

tracks.title: Streaming & Event Data Engineer
tracks.who: You build Kafka, Flink and CDC pipelines.
tracks.watchOut: Kafka 4.x is KRaft-only; drop ZooKeeper-based examples you find elsewhere.

tracks.title: Search & Retrieval Engineer
tracks.who: You build product search, relevance ranking and vector retrieval.
tracks.watchOut: Hybrid search (keyword + vector) with re-ranking is the default per `.claude/rules/rag-vector-standards.md`.

tracks.title: Prompt Engineer & AI Evaluator
tracks.who: You design prompts, evaluation sets and quality gates for LLM features.
tracks.watchOut: Measure prompt changes on a fixed eval set; the evaluation architecture is in `reports/Agent skills evaluation architecture.md`.

tracks.title: AI Safety & LLM Red Team
tracks.who: You test and harden LLM apps against prompt injection, jailbreaks and data leaks.
tracks.watchOut: Test only systems you own or are authorized to test; keep findings and payloads inside your evaluation suite.

tracks.title: GPU Kernel & Inference Engineer
tracks.who: You write or tune CUDA/Triton kernels and LLM serving performance.
tracks.watchOut: PTX/SASS skills are for profiling-driven work; most teams stop at Triton or vendor libraries.

tracks.title: Low-Latency & HFT Engineer
tracks.who: You build trading or networking systems where microseconds matter.
tracks.watchOut: Measure with hardware timestamps on your own hardware; do not trust published latency numbers.

tracks.title: IoT & Edge Engineer
tracks.who: You connect devices, run code at the edge and ship ML to small hardware.
tracks.watchOut: Read `.claude/rules/misra-c-standards.md` for firmware and `.claude/rules/crypto-deprecation.md` for device credentials.

tracks.title: DeFi Protocol Engineer
tracks.who: You build lending, AMM or vault protocols.
tracks.watchOut: Oracle manipulation and flash-loan attacks are the classic DeFi failures; use TWAP or multi-source oracles with freshness checks.

tracks.title: Zero-Knowledge & Cryptography Engineer
tracks.who: You build ZK circuits, proof systems or cryptographic protocols.
tracks.watchOut: Read `.claude/rules/zk-circuit-rules.md`: unconstrained signals are the most common ZK bug.

tracks.title: Quantum Computing Researcher
tracks.who: You learn or prototype quantum algorithms and post-quantum migration.
tracks.watchOut: `quantum-computing/quantum-error-correction` and `fundamental-truths/quantum-error-correction` overlap; the first is practical, the second theoretical.

tracks.title: QA Automation Engineer
tracks.who: You build end-to-end, visual and regression suites that run in CI.
tracks.watchOut: Three Playwright-flavoured skills overlap (`quality-e2e-testing`, `e2e-playwright`, `frontend/e2e-testing`); keep the first two.

tracks.title: SEO & Web Growth Engineer
tracks.who: You grow organic traffic and conversion with fast, well-structured pages.
tracks.watchOut: INP replaced FID as a Core Web Vital in 2024; ignore advice that still targets FID.

tracks.title: Legacy Modernization Lead
tracks.who: You move monoliths and old platforms to modern architecture without stopping the business.
tracks.watchOut: Strangler-fig migrations need regression tests around the old behavior before the first cut-over.

tracks.title: Microservices Engineer
tracks.who: You split systems into services and keep them reliable in production.
tracks.watchOut: Start with a modular monolith if the domain boundaries are not clear yet; `backend/universal/microservices` explains when to split.

tracks.title: GraphQL API Engineer
tracks.who: You design, federate and optimize GraphQL APIs.
tracks.watchOut: Add query depth and cost limits before exposing a public GraphQL endpoint.

tracks.title: Agile Coach & Scrum Master
tracks.who: You improve how teams plan, deliver and learn.
tracks.watchOut: `management/agile-scrum` duplicates `agile-scrum-kanban`; keep the Kanban one.

profiles.title: Solo founder: web MVP in weeks
profiles.situation: One person, one web product, ship fast.
profiles.notes: Add `saas` Level 1 once you charge money; add `quality` Level 1 before the first paying customer.

profiles.title: Seed-stage SaaS team (3–8 engineers)
profiles.situation: A small team with paying customers and a growing codebase.
profiles.notes: Swap `fullstack` for your stack tracks (for example `react` + `python-backend`) once the stack is settled.

profiles.title: Scale-up platform team
profiles.situation: Several product teams need a reliable, observable platform.
profiles.notes: Add `finops` Level 1 when the cloud bill becomes a board topic.

profiles.title: Enterprise modernization program
profiles.situation: Moving a large legacy estate to cloud and services.
profiles.notes: Replace `java-kotlin-backend` with `dotnet` for Microsoft shops.

profiles.title: AI product startup
profiles.situation: An LLM-powered product with RAG and agents.
profiles.notes: Add `ai-safety` Level 1 before opening the product to untrusted users.

profiles.title: Internal AI agents and tools
profiles.situation: Agents that act on internal systems for employees.
profiles.notes: Put human approval in front of every tool that changes production; see `.claude/rules/agent-persona-design.md`.

profiles.title: Data platform team
profiles.situation: A central team running pipelines, warehouse and streaming.
profiles.notes: Add `mlops` Level 1 when models start consuming the platform's data.

profiles.title: ML product team
profiles.situation: Data scientists and ML engineers shipping models to users.
profiles.notes: Add `gpu-kernels` Level 1 only if serving cost or latency is the bottleneck.

profiles.title: Mobile-first consumer app
profiles.situation: One cross-platform app plus a backend and growth loop.
profiles.notes: Swap `react-native` for `flutter` if your team writes Dart.

profiles.title: Native mobile studio
profiles.situation: Separate native iOS and Android apps.
profiles.notes: Add `design-ux` Level 1 if designers work in the same repository.

profiles.title: Indie game (Unity)
profiles.situation: A small team shipping a single-player or light multiplayer game.
profiles.notes: Swap `unity` for `godot` or `unreal` to match your engine.

profiles.title: Online multiplayer game
profiles.situation: Authoritative servers, matchmaking and live operations.
profiles.notes: Add your engine track (`unity`, `unreal` or `godot`) at Level 1 for the client side.

profiles.title: Fintech or payments product
profiles.situation: Money movement, ledgers, compliance and fraud risk.
profiles.notes: Read `.claude/rules/distributed-safeguards.md`: idempotency on every money-moving endpoint.

profiles.title: Web3 protocol team
profiles.situation: Smart contracts holding real value.
profiles.notes: Plan an external audit before mainnet; the skills do not replace one.

profiles.title: Security team
profiles.situation: AppSec, detection and compliance in one small team.
profiles.notes: Add `ai-safety` Level 1 if the company ships LLM features.

profiles.title: Open-source library
profiles.situation: A public package with contributors and releases.
profiles.notes: Add your language track (for example `rust` or `python-backend`) at Level 1.

profiles.title: Agency or freelancer building client websites
profiles.situation: Many fast, accessible, search-friendly marketing sites.
profiles.notes: Use `react` Level 1 instead of `modern-frontend` for Next.js-based clients.

profiles.title: New tech lead on an existing codebase
profiles.situation: You inherited a codebase and need to steer it.
profiles.notes: Add the stack track of the codebase at Level 1.

profiles.title: Learning to code
profiles.situation: A student or career switcher building solid habits.
profiles.notes: Move to one product track (for example `react` or `python-backend`) after your first finished project.

profiles.title: Low-latency trading system
profiles.situation: Market data, order routing and microsecond budgets.
profiles.notes: Add `compliance` Level 1 for regulated markets.
